_what: How an uploaded video is made one playable format at ingest (src/ingest-normalization.mjs reads it). `target` is the one format every video is kept playable as. Each `convert` row is a type that is not that format: its extension, whether it carries no sound (`silent`, so the runner drops audio and makes the size even), and the words used for the type. `ffmpeg_args` are the arguments an ffmpeg-like runner takes to make the target (`{input}` and `{output}` are filled with the runner's own paths). A type with no row is kept as it came, and the answer lists what Trillion does convert. `convert_max_bytes` is the largest file one conversion takes; a bigger one is kept as it came and the answer says why. Changing a row changes ingest; nothing is compiled.

words.kept: {label} is already the one playable format, so it was kept as it came.
words.convert: {from} is not kept as it came: it is made {to} so every screen can play it.
words.too_big: This {from} file is {size} MiB, more than the {limit} MiB one conversion takes, so it was kept as it came and may not play everywhere. Converts: {supported}.
words.not_listed: {type} is not a video type Trillion converts, so it was kept as it came. Converts: {supported}; kept as is: {target}.

source.from: Spatial's add_video text: 'Supported: mp4, mov, webm, webp, gif, avi' and 'Couldn't convert that ... file to mp4' (REA finding F-0835)
